analysis.investment_thesis: CarTrade's online automotive marketplace — CarWale, BikeWale, OLX India, Shriram Automall — is a concept Lynch would understand from simply observing how Indians increasingly research and trade cars digitally; revenue grew 31% in FY25 to ₹641 Cr and operating margins are a healthy 33%. However, ROE of just 6.24%, P/S of 12x, and a long history of unprofitable operation make this an expensive bet on a story still proving itself.
key_strengths: Revenue accelerating: 313→364→490→641 Cr (FY22-25) with 31% growth in FY25 — the platform is gaining traction
Asset-light model with near-zero capex (₹5 Cr FY25) and 33% operating margins, producing ₹171 Cr OCF in FY25 after years of low conversion
Multi-brand platform covering new cars, used cars, two-wheelers, auctions, and OLX India — diversified digital automotive ecosystem
key_risks: ROE of 6.24% and ROCE of 7.59% are unacceptable for a platform business — the company earns barely above cost of capital on its equity
Net profit history is wildly erratic: -₹121 Cr (FY22), +₹40 Cr (FY23), +₹20 Cr (FY24), +₹145 Cr (FY25) — FY25 jump partly driven by ₹70 Cr other income
P/S of 11.98x on revenue of ₹641 Cr is rich; no promoter holding disclosed, with FII owning 64.6% — exit risk if sentiment shifts
red_flags: FY24 net profit of only ₹20 Cr on revenue of ₹490 Cr — operating leverage has been extremely elusive for two decades
FY25 OCF of ₹171 Cr is encouraging but OCF was just ₹16 Cr in FY24 — one good year doesn't make a trend
No promoter shareholding reported — concentrated FII ownership at 64.6% creates vulnerability to institutional selling
analysis.detailed_analysis: Lynch loves platform businesses in growing markets, and India's used-car digitization is a real trend you can observe in any metro. CarTrade has built real brands and the FY25 acceleration is promising — 31% revenue growth, positive OCF, expanding operating margins. The problem is that this company has been around since 2000 and still can't consistently earn its cost of capital; ROE of 6% is a damning indictment of capital allocation over two decades. At P/S of 12x, the market is pricing in aggressive future profitability that has historically not materialized. Lynch would say: 'I like the story, but show me two more years of consistent earnings before I pay 12 times sales for it.' Worth watching at ₹1,200-1,300, not owning at ₹1,858.
